newsitem.title: HUNGARY: DENSO TO BUILD $100M FACTORY IN HUNGARY.
newsitem.headline: DENSO TO BUILD $100M FACTORY IN HUNGARY.

text.p: Japanese car parts manufacturer Denso Corporation is to build its first European diesel engine injection pump factory in Hungary, Hungarian ecomonic news agency MTI-Econews reported on Tuesday.
Construction work on the $100 million plant will start this September and the 26,000 square metre plant factory is scheduled to start production by June 1999 with a workforce of 400.

Denso International Europe managing director Nobuyuki Fujitani said the factory, to be built at Szekesfehervar, in western Hungary, will have annual capacity of 180,000 injection pumps by the year 2000.
Denso expects to make a return on its investment within five years of operation, Fujitani said.
The entire output of the Szekesfehervar plant will go for export but Fujitani declined to name potential partner companies.

However, Laszlo Nemenyi, president of the Hungarian ministry of industry's trade promotion arm ITD Hungary, said one potential major customer would be the Isuzu factory in Poland which is scheduled to commence production by 2000.
